narrative.p01: A working private analytics demo exists. October 17 Phase 1 is additionally accepted locally on schema 0027 and is not deployed; the live private demo remains on 0020. Noncommercial use and all eight production gates remain unchanged.
narrative.p02: Governed files, dashboards/chat, measured relationships, saved work, basic and opt-in advanced forecasts, refresh/alerts, audit, support/usage, anomaly checks, budget choices and explicit what-if scenarios. Field diagrams, private context, protected portable results and row/column policies are delivered.
narrative.p03: Production identity/security acceptance; payments and paid subscriptions; live external connectors and embedding; representative advanced-method acceptance and complete production operations. Native registration and price-free internal plans are locally delivered; Phase 2 final acceptance remains pending.
narrative.p04: Done means the requested function is implemented and supported by tests within its stated local or private-demo scope. Local acceptance does not mean deployment. Partly done means a subset works or required setup/acceptance remains. Not yet means the end-to-end capability is absent. Every row states its limits.
narrative.p05: We count the VC’s original 64 feature lines, retaining overlaps such as billing and onboarding. Combined requests are not split to inflate the score. These are feature counts, not a percentage of engineering effort or competitor parity. The instruction about predictive/prescriptive claims is assessed separately.
narrative.p06: “Company registration” means software account signup, not legal incorporation.
narrative.p07: Guided reading preserves answers. Pattern requests calculate measured associations and show weak evidence honestly. AI explanations remain fallible; daily assumptions are not learned forecasts.
narrative.p08: ExecPlus overlaps with parts of the upload → question → dashboard experience. It has not reached the connected-data breadth or commercial completeness of either target.
narrative.p09: This documents capabilities, not hands-on performance or percentage parity. Editions and setup differ. The comparison was reviewed on 5 October 2026; the separate October 6 interface-reference review is recorded in E13.
narrative.p10: Conversational analytics, AI dashboards and governed queries are shared capabilities, not proven unique advantages. Our strongest current demonstration is the combination of retained files, reviewed meanings, exact calculations, replayable answers, document citations and visible request activity. A shared evaluation would be needed to claim better quality or speed.
narrative.p11: Do not assume every vendor catalog tile is live: Polymer labels some connectors “Coming Soon”. The VC requested accounting and advanced-analysis features are not automatically capabilities of both target products. [P1]
narrative.p12: Most unfinished items are already planned or deliberately deferred. “Not yet” does not mean they were forgotten; it means no complete feature is available today.
narrative.p13: Native customer signup, password sessions and operator recovery now pass local tests while existing demo tokens remain supported. Verified-email recovery, deployment identity controls and independent security/privacy review still need acceptance.
narrative.p14: PDF dashboards/reports, exact Excel results, PNG charts and CSV/evidence bundles are delivered with authorization and preserved source evidence. Actual email delivery remains a separate external dependency.
narrative.p15: Start with read-only Google Sheets and an approved PostgreSQL source. Add accounting systems and BigQuery only after safe connection/refresh behavior is verified.
narrative.p16: Internal administration, support and usage reporting remain delivered. Local native setup and administrator-controlled tier allowances now pass real backend/UI tests. Payments, subscriptions, payment-derived upgrades and real email delivery remain unfinished.
narrative.p17: Representative evaluations, identity/security, recovery and provider privacy must pass. Private-demo evidence does not clear production launch gates.
narrative.p18: The independent remaining-work instruction is active. Phase 1 is locally accepted on 0027; Phase 2 final verification remains pending. The live 0020 private demo is unchanged. External integrations and production launch require their own reviewed evidence.
narrative.p19: PDF/Excel exports remain Done within the tested scope. Native signup and internal tier allowances are locally verified; production identity acceptance, payments and paid-plan configuration remain unfinished. No payment activation is simulated.
narrative.p20: Representative customer examples and labels; retrieval/citation quality; a tested production search provider; backup/restore proof; model quality/speed/cost comparison; hosted-provider privacy; real email delivery; and production identity/security. A successful demo does not close these checks. [E7]
narrative.p21: Durable chat requests with real activity, reconnect/resume, cancellation and Simple/Expert views.
narrative.p22: These extras are not added to the 64-item score. The optional AI judge was evaluated and rejected; it is not a delivered runtime capability.
narrative.p23: Advertise tested descriptive analytics, basic forecasts and bounded conditional analysis with limitations. Do not claim full predictive or prescriptive analytics.
narrative.p24: Live web 5c48d3c and API/jobs 867c5a0 remain on schema 0020. The accepted October 17 local Phase 1 candidate reaches 0027 with native accounts, guided setup, price-free plans and operational checks; it has not been activated on the VPS. Personal phase2 includes phase3 data-reading commit 2a93080.
narrative.p25: Phase 1 reconciliation accounts for all 2,580 collected backend cases with latest passing executions and maps all 37 original completed requirements. Nine initial harness failures remain recorded; five generated-XLSX node aliases were verified from identical uncompressed fixtures. This is combined full/focused coverage, not one clean run. Frontend checks, builds, offline browser journeys and targeted onboarding/allowance paths pass; three model-dependent journeys remain skipped. Phase 2 final regression and all eight production gates remain open.
narrative.p26: Current evidence outranks old phase labels. Complete applies only to the tested scope.
narrative.p27: One score per original VC line, in order; keep overlapping requests separate.
narrative.p28: Combined requests need all key parts; variance and root cause are different.
narrative.p29: Partial is not done. Delivered features retain each row’s stated limits.
narrative.p30: Checklist counts do not measure effort, cost, time or complete competitor parity.
narrative.p31: Clickable references for the comparison table. Reviewed 5 October 2026; these are vendor documentation and marketing claims, not independent performance or security validation.
narrative.p32: Feature availability can vary by edition, version, configuration and permissions. Missing mention on a website is not proof a competitor lacks a feature. We did not assign either vendor a 64-item completion score or infer all accounting/forecasting features from generic “AI analytics” language.
narrative.p33: ThoughtSpot permission claims here refer to documented governed-query execution; this is not a blanket assessment of every AI context or memory path. Polymer scheduled emails are documented; threshold-alert support was not established by the pages reviewed.
narrative.p34: Suggested positioning is our inference: demonstrate a focused, evidence-backed data-partner workflow, then prove any quality, speed or usability advantage with the same disclosed datasets and tasks for all products.
